scoring_notes.SCI: State Commitment Index. Federal budget activity + state-linked contractor starts + 2% mortgage volume as state expenditure.
scoring_notes.track_a: Private market signal. Non-state developer entry + cash DKP transactions (non-mortgage) + asking price momentum. Mariupol penalised: Bellingcat/Shumanov confirm near-zero genuine private entry.
scoring_notes.track_b: Residential outcome signal. Secondary listing depth (Domclick counts) + buyer permanence score (PSB/VTB disclosures) + rental-to-purchase ratio (estimated where marked). | Aug 26 — Donbas Track B watch condition (Donetsk 58, Luhansk 54, both held). Two independent signals this window point downward, both partisan-sourced and neither corroborated: the National Resistance Center (Aug 9) reports occupation administrations across the occupied territories exploiting unemployment and months-long wage arrears to recruit civilians into the Russian army under false pretenses; ATESH (Aug 26) reports commanders of the 70th Motorized Rifle Division selling military fuel allocations to civilians in Donetsk, Luhansk and Rostov-on-Don at prices from 300 rubles per litre. If the ATESH report is corroborated it would be the first confirmed acute fuel-access failure in the Donbas cities at Crimea intensity, and grey-market fuel reaching the captive population matters more than the same signal in Crimea: per the README’s Donbas caveat, Track B there measures a residual self-selected population whose participation reflects a prior political commitment, so movement in it is categorically more acute than movement elsewhere. Three Galaktika shopping-centre fires in a single month (Makiivka Aug 9–10, Yenakiieve Aug 14, Donetsk Aug 16, the last with eyewitness drone flyovers) add commercial-stock attrition alongside the already-logged Aug 8 school and kindergarten closures. Track B is nonetheless the climate dial and moves on Domclick listing depth and PSB/VTB buyer composition, not on news or partisan reporting. Explicit corroboration trigger for the next cycle: a second independent source on the fuel diversion, or any Domclick listing-count or PSB disclosure movement in Donetsk or Luhansk. If either arrives, move both to 56/52 and note that the trigger was pre-registered here. | Sep 9 — WATCH CONDITION OPENED BY DAVID FOR TRIGGER REVIEW. Values HOLD at Donetsk 58, Luhansk 54; the numeric move to 56/52 is gated and is NOT executed in this package. The original trigger language above is preserved verbatim; this is an append, not a rewrite. THE CONDITION HAS NOW RUN FOUR CYCLES UNRESOLVED (08-27, 08-29, 08-31, 09-01), and the evidence arriving keeps failing the trigger ON SPECIFICATION RATHER THAN ON SUBSTANCE: the four-oblast blackout (Aug 27–28) was rejected as grid disruption rather than fuel-diversion corroboration; the EU Delegation "Eating Last" report (Aug 31) is consistent with the condition but meets neither branch; and the Galaktika Mariupol strike (Sep 6–7) is the fourth chain location destroyed in a month, with the co-located station reportedly the LAST GALAKTIKA-BRAND FUEL STATION IN OCCUPIED DONETSK OBLAST. THE ANALYTICAL QUESTION, STATED PLAINLY: the Galaktika sequence introduces a FUEL-RETAIL INFRASTRUCTURE dimension that the original trigger — written around fuel DIVERSION and listing/buyer data — did not anticipate. The condition may now be filtering out the evidence actually arriving. Carried to the v5.1 queue as a candidate Track B input dimension. SECOND BRANCH TESTED SEP 9, RESULT REPORTED AND NOT SCORED: a live Domclick pull returned Donetsk apartments 651–652 against a last committed 380 (2026-06-10) and Luhansk houses 1,090 against 974 — both moved, and Donetsk crossed the independently pre-registered donetsk_apartments_surge alert of 600 in domclick_listings.json. THE BASELINE IS THREE MONTHS OLD, NOT A SAME-CYCLE COMPARISON: the scraper has not run since 2026-06-10, so this is drift over one quarter rather than movement within a cycle. Whether that satisfies "movement" as pre-registered is David’s ruling; no dial was touched.
scoring_notes.composite: SCI × 0.4 + Track A × 0.6. Weighted blend of state commitment and private market signal.
scoring_notes.spread: Track B minus Composite (SCI×0.4 + A×0.6). Positive = residential confidence LEADS state+private composite. Negative = composite OUTPACES residential reality — the fragility signal.
scoring_notes.data_quality: real = sourced and dateable. estimated = calibrated from anchors. uncertain = low-confidence estimate. | HISTORY MONTH ROLLED 2026-06 -> 2026-09 on 2026-09-09, David’s ruling, overriding the work package’s standing instruction not to re-key. THE SERIES NOW SKIPS 2026-07 AND 2026-08, AND THAT GAP IS THE HONEST SHAPE OF THE DATA: no July or August reading was ever taken. Every entry before the last carries an empty note; only the last carries one, and those notes record dated updates running through Aug 26 (Mariupol: "Aug 9: Track A 31→29"). The entry keyed 2026-06 was the LIVE entry, opened in June and maintained continuously since, so re-keying states what it already was rather than asserting a new reading. APPENDING WAS REJECTED because a new entry needs values and CC does not set them; carrying the same values forward would have asserted "no change June to September", which those same notes falsify. NO SCORE MOVED IN THIS OPERATION — SCI, Track A, Track B, composite and spread are byte-identical for all five cities, and Donetsk 58 / Luhansk 54 remain held per the gated WP-4b. TWO VISIBLE CONSEQUENCES, NEITHER A DEFECT: the month scrubber now reads "... Apr 26, May 26, Sep 26", showing the gap rather than hiding it; and the Key Events legend, which renders only events whose date matches a chart axis label, now surfaces 2026-09 events on the composite and spread charts. JULY AND AUGUST EVENTS REMAIN INVISIBLE THERE — no axis label exists for them, and this roll does not fix that. SEPARATELY AND NOT TOUCHED: refinery_pressure.json, civilian_confidence.json and occupation_financial_pressure.json carry the identical freeze at 2026-06 under the field name `monthly_readings` rather than `history`, with the same pattern of an August-and-September log appended into a June-keyed entry.

history.note: Aug 9: Track A 31→29. BBC Verify Aug 7: 34,002 unique addresses flagged for expropriation or confiscation across occupied territories — 14,308 in Mariupol alone. Property rights framework breakdown: owners must hold Russian passport and return within 30 days to contest confiscation — practically impossible for displaced Ukrainians. USF strikes on four Mariupol power substations (Myrna 330kV, Misto-2, Misto-4, Misto-11) as part of Crimean Switch Off operation — energy infrastructure essential to any private market activity directly targeted. HUR Jul 20: Russian planning documents project Mariupol-Kalmius population growth from 228,000 to 518,000 by 2035 through Russian resettlement — genuine private market being replaced by administered settler economy. | Aug 9: Track B 24→22. BBC Verify 14,308 Mariupol addresses flagged for expropriation directly undermines buyer permanence — property one ‘buys’ subject to administrative reallocation. Second phase housing redistribution Jul 21: 3,000+ apartments allocated to regime-loyal residents (veterans, large families, public-sector employees) requiring Russian passports. Kherson Oblast occupation head Saldo announces redistribution of ‘ownerless’ housing to war veterans and civil servants. Ukraine GUR warns policies constitute ‘ethnocide and colonization.’ Occupied Donetsk closing schools and kindergartens Aug 8 — civic services failure expanding. | Aug 26: Track A holds at 29 — deliberately, against new transaction data. DW’s Aug 14–15 investigation is the richest Mariupol market evidence in the dataset: contractor Su-2007 has completed multiple 12–15 storey blocks (Leningradsky Kvartal) on cleared sites where residents were killed or displaced in 2022; apartments sell at 7.5–10M rubles (€104,000+); Mariupol leads all occupied cities in mortgage loan volume per Russian banking statistics; prices are up roughly one third year-on-year per economist Vyacheslav Shiryaev. Every one of those transactions runs through the 2% state mortgage, capped at 6M rubles, requiring Russian citizenship and a 2% deposit, with buyers drawn from security personnel, officials and military logistics workers. Under Methodology v3.0 (Bellingcat Nov 2025 / Shumanov) this is state expenditure projecting permanence, not private capital expressing confidence, and it belongs to SCI. Scoring it into Track A would collapse the SCI/Track A separation that the methodology exists to maintain. Recorded here so the hold is legible as a judgment rather than an oversight. | Aug 26: Track B 22→21. DW confirms buyers are insuring their mortgages against war risks — the settler buyer population is itself pricing impermanence, which is the most direct Track B signal available and the first time the buyer side has been observed hedging. Original residents received no units in the replacement stock and some were ordered out of surviving apartments into hostels or the city outskirts; approximately 900 further apartments are listed for redistribution. Infrastructure: Aug 8 substation strike caused confirmed power and water failure with occupation head Koltsov acknowledging inability to fully restore services; Aug 13–14 USF struck four Mariupol 110 kV substations (Misto-3, NS-2, Illich, Misto-6) and the GRS-1 gas distribution station. Mariupol City Council has won $34.12M across 16 judgments against Russia for destroyed municipal property with 40 further assessments pending (UA News Aug 17) — the legal overhang on title is now quantified and growing. | Aug 26: SCI holds at 91. EJIL:Talk (Aug 26) confirms the 2% programme runs to 2030 with 6,000+ loans issued by late 2025 and continued growth, and that Federal Constitutional Law No. 4-FKZ (Dec 2025) enables redistribution of confiscated Ukrainian property to Russian citizens; official territorial planning projects an additional 113,800 residents across the occupied oblasts by 2045. This is consistent with 91 rather than a step-change above it.

history.note: Jun 21 AM: Track A 54→50, composite 57→55, spread −11→−9. Hotel booking collapse confirmed worsening (31% overall, 40% Sevastopol). | Jun 21 PM: Track B 46→38, spread −9→−17. First substantive Track B movement of the monitoring period. Total civilian fuel access suspension (Aksyonov/Razvozhayev, 9am Jun 21) directly undermines the residential-permanence premise — 30-year mortgage commitment hard to rationalize where legal civilian fuel purchase is currently impossible. Composite stays 55 (SCI and Track A unchanged). RPI held at 96 — fuel ban is distribution/access policy downstream of existing RPI pressure, not new refinery/export infrastructure damage. | Jun 24: Track A 50→47, Track B 38→35, composite 55→53, spread −17→−18. Sevastopol full city blackout after main substation destroyed overnight Jun 23–24. North Crimean Canal railway bridge destroyed (SSO two-phase strike). Black Sea Fleet families evacuating to Novorossiysk. Tourism/summer camp season effectively cancelled. Multi-modal civilian infrastructure failure: fuel + power + transport simultaneously. | Jul 3: Track B 35→33, spread −18→−20. Geographic spread of infrastructure failure confirmed beyond Sevastopol: Armyansk without power and water 2+ days, Feodosia municipal district significant outages, Sevastopol power restored then re-cut within 24 hours. Peninsula-wide failure, not city-specific. 3,500-vehicle queue confirmed at Kerch Bridge (Inkorr Jul 2). Residential permanence premise further eroded by sustained multi-city collapse. | Jul 9: Track A 47→44. Kyiv Post/Korshak reports Crimea real estate prices down 30–50% since January 2026 during peak summer season — confirmed demand collapse. Tourism reservations down 79% in June; rail and ferry suspended. Private market confidence in active collapse, not mere stagnation. | Jul 9: Track B →30, spread →−21. Peninsula-wide Crimea blackout Jul 6 (Krymenergo confirmed regionwide). Sevastopol kindergartens cut from 74 to 24 operating — first-order civic services failure. Fuel rationing confirmed in all four occupied oblasts. Multi-commodity food shortages confirmed (sugar, flour, cereals, salt, pasta). Grey market fuel via Telegram/Avito. Aksyonov Jul 8: crisis 'open-ended,' fuel unavailability on certain days permanent. Residents describing 'survival mode' (Le Monde Jul 9). 30–50% real estate price collapse corroborates residential permanence rejection. | Jul 9: MTCS at 80 (acute boundary — threshold is >80; band remains Fragility Zone). Base 78 + OFP +2 = 80. ECS at ceiling (100). Crimea in active evacuation. Behavioral change underway, not anticipated — state of emergency, civilian exodus, industrial shutdowns, civic services failure all confirmed. | Jul 17: Track A 44→42. Don-Azov Canal suspended Jul 10–11; Sea of Azov vessel count fell from 132 to 43 (55% AIS transponder decline); maritime blockade of Crimea supply routes now complete — land corridors and sea routes simultaneously closed. No new private market transaction data but macro environment for any private activity has materially worsened beyond Jul 9 baseline. | Jul 17: Track B 30→28. Confirmed persistence and deepening of civilian infrastructure failure: water supply limited to one hour daily in some areas (Jul 11); farms halting mechanized operations due to combined electricity and fuel failures (Chubarov/ISW Jul 14); rotating 2-on/6-off blackouts in Sevastopol (Razvozhayev Jul 14); transformer cannibalization — ATESH Jul 14 reports Russian authorities removing transformers from idle Northern Crimean Canal pumping stations to replace destroyed substations, spare stocks exhausted; VTB ATM withdrawal limits reduced for Crimea customers. These are not disruptions — they are the new baseline. Residential permanence premise structurally impaired beyond prior floor. | Jul 17: MTCS crosses acute threshold (>80). Base 78 + OFP +4 = 82. OFP modulator advances from +2 to +4 as fiscal pressure crosses into meaningful-strain band. ECS at ceiling (100). Crimea in active evacuation — maritime blockade complete, water/power/fuel simultaneously failed, agricultural and emergency services affected. Behavioral change confirmed and deepening, not anticipated. | Aug 9: Track A 42→40. Riddle/Trickett (Jul 31) independent analytical confirmation of complete private market collapse — sustained multi-week, no recovery trajectory. Novorossiysk large-ship sailings down 38% in July; tanker runs down by half; only four tankers loaded at Novorossiysk in week ending Jul 26. Russian grain exporters warn systematic strikes ‘could soon lead to complete blocking of export corridors.’ No private capital entry rationale exists under current conditions. | Aug 9: Track B 28→26. Confirmed persistence and structural deepening: Russian government formally decreed suspension of Housing Code late-payment penalties across all four occupied oblasts (Jul 29) — administrative confirmation civilian economic capacity to sustain normal household obligations has collapsed. Feodosia high-voltage substation on Feodosia–Kerch highway destroyed Jul 27–28, disrupting power across occupied Crimea. Water supply emergency declared peninsula-wide in response. Sky News Jul 31: hundreds of thousands without electricity for days, concurrent water shortages and fuel rationing. ACLED confirms 205 vessels struck and R-280 network-dismantling campaign expanded — maritime alternative permanently closed. Residential permanence premise has no remaining rational basis at any normal time horizon. | Aug 9: MTCS 82 (holds). OFP advances to 70 (band ceiling); modulator holds at +4. NWF depletion confirmed at monthly anchor — liquid assets 1.8% GDP, gold 71% depleted from pre-war. Crimea Track A/B both down, Mariupol Track A/B both down on BBC Verify expropriation data and sustained infrastructure failure. ECS at ceiling (100). Weighted corridor REP 56.41 → Base 78; rounding holds base at 78 despite spread deterioration across three cities. Next OFP threshold (71+) triggers modulator jump to +6 — watch for liquid assets approaching 1% GDP or confirmed emissions-supported OFZ auction failure. | Aug 26: Track A 40→38. Crimean Wind (Aug 19, via ISW) reports hotel occupancy in occupied Crimea down roughly 35% in July and 30% in August [unverified — Ukrainian partisan source]. August is the month in which any Crimea private-market recovery would have to appear; peak season produced no bounce off the Aug 9 floor. NPR Aug 13 provides independent English-language ground truth — a resident describing ‘no gasoline, no fuel, no power,’ with stores and banks closed. Fuel availability nationally at 28% of stations (ISW Aug 19, citing Izvestia/GdeBENZ); Rosgvardia paramilitary units deployed to fuel stations across Russia and occupied Crimea to manage civil unrest. No new Restate.ru transaction data — see Step 10. | Aug 26: Track B 26→25. Water cut off in 35 settlements and gasoline out at most peninsula filling stations again as of Aug 16 (intent.press); occupation authorities planning to replace hot school meals with dry rations (intent.press Aug 17) — civic services failure now reaching statutory child provisioning, a category not previously logged. Mandatory Euro-2/Euro-3 fuel is causing civilian vehicle breakdowns (ISW Aug 21) — the rationing regime is now damaging the private capital stock, not merely restricting access to it. Krymenergo and Sevastopolenergo on restricted schedules; Balaklava TPP struck Aug 13–14 with Razvozhayev confirming city-wide outages. | Aug 26: Crimea spread holds at −23 despite both tracks falling. Track A and Track B declined together, so the composite fell in step with residential reality and the fragility gap is flat. This is a finding, not an omission: Crimea’s deterioration this cycle is uniform across state, private and residential signals rather than divergent, which is what a market completing its exit looks like rather than one still separating. | Aug 26: MTCS 82→84. Base holds at 78; OFP advances 70→74, crossing into the 71–85 band and lifting the modulator +4→+6. The base is unchanged because Crimea’s spread held at −23 (Track A and Track B fell together) while Mariupol widened to −33 and Berdiansk to −15 — corridor REP moved only 56.41→56.76 and rounding absorbed it. All MTCS movement this cycle is attributable to the fiscal modulator, not to the real estate sector. ECS remains at ceiling (100), RPI and CCI both at 100. OFP crossing was made on Minfin’s Jan–Jul deficit at 1.7× the full-year target rather than on any of the three triggers named Aug 9, none of which fired. Next thresholds: OFP above 85 lifts the modulator to +8; a corridor REP above ~58 would lift the base to 79. Watch the ~Sept 3 Minfin NWF disclosure for the liquid-assets-below-1%-of-GDP condition, and the Donbas Track B corroboration trigger recorded in scoring_notes.

berdiansk.notes: Thin data. All estimates. Port opened to international shipping Aug 2025.

history.note: Aug 9: Track B 14→12. Complete power and water failure Jul 24 (ATESH/UNN — confirmed by multiple sources). Aug 1 energy infrastructure strike leaving part of Berdiansk without power. Infrastructure failure now recurring, not episodic. Residential permanence premise undermined by simultaneous multi-utility failure. | Aug 26: Track B 12→11. Fourth and fifth confirmed rounds of energy infrastructure strikes in six weeks: energy hubs struck Aug 10–11 as part of a 43-target USF operation; at least seven substations across 150 kV and 110 kV tiers struck Aug 13–14 under Crimean Switch Off, including repeated hits on the Berdiansk and Morska nodes; electrical substations near Berdiansk struck again in the Aug 17–22 window (ISW Aug 23); fuel, ammunition and logistics depots at Berdiansk and Prymorsk struck Aug 24–25. Infrastructure failure in Berdiansk is now continuous rather than episodic or even recurring — the city has no observed interval of restored normal service across the period. Held to −1 rather than the −2 suggested by the Aug 14 digest, on the discipline that Berdiansk carries data_quality ‘uncertain’ and a 0.7 city weight; a two-point move on thin data would propagate into MTCS with more confidence than the sourcing supports.

Rostov Oblast declares a state of emergency citing Azov–Black Sea shipping disruption
YANOS refinery struck (Slavneft-YANOS, Yaroslavl — Moscow Times / Kyiv Independent / Censor.NET Aug 28)
Russia extends the fuel export ban through September 30 — policy confirmation of sustained domestic supply stress (ISW Aug 29)

NV Ukraine Crimea investigation: 450-ruble grey-market fuel, 211% official fuel price inflation in July, 30% food price rises, civic service collapse, real-estate demand contraction; independently confirms the Sevastopol 2-hours-on/6-hours-off blackout schedule and water outages across northern Crimea (NV Ukraine Aug 29)

NV Ukraine: first named-source confirmation of a residential price decline in occupied Crimea — down 28%, from 180,000 to 130,000 rubles/m²; settlers documented attempting to relocate families off the peninsula (NV Ukraine Aug 29)

Kirishi/KINEF refinery (Leningrad Oblast) struck overnight Aug 29–30 — Russia’s SECOND-LARGEST refinery at roughly 20M tonnes/year (~400,000 bpd), over 6% of national refining capacity, and a supplier of military fuel. ALL CRUDE PROCESSING HALTED after the AVT-6 unit (22,860 t/day, ~40% of the refinery’s capacity) and the AT-1 unit (4,860 t/day, ~8%) were damaged; at least the sixth reported Ukrainian strike on the facility. Struck the same night as the Yeysk military airfield (Bloomberg / Reuters via MarineLink / Euromaidan Press / Kyiv Post / Militarnyi Aug 30)
Grain rerouting away from Russian ports confirmed, with Akkon, Arkas and MSC exiting Russian port calls — structural export-corridor rerouting rather than temporary disruption (Reuters/Meduza Aug 31)
EU Delegation "Eating Last" report documents barter economies, informal food networks and shadow survival economies across occupied Donetsk and Luhansk (EU Delegation Aug 31)
Christian Science Monitor Crimea ground-truth report: 20-day power outages, refrigeration failure destroying agricultural produce, near-zero tourism, supplier withdrawal (CSM Aug 31)
The Insider / TVP World / Vot Tak: 61.4bn rubles in Russian state bank loans extended for Mariupol housing projects, with developer profits estimated above market norms (Sep 1)
Crimea fuel shortage persists on the day of Aksyonov’s publicized supply-improvement promise; ration coupons reappear in Alushta; double-price charging confirmed in Dzhankoy (Intent Press Sep 1)
Sberbank CEO Gref publicly attributes Russian inflation to refinery strike losses — highest-status Russian-source confirmation to date of the strike campaign’s fiscal impact (Reuters Sep 3)
Crimea fuel rationing tightened to four-hour daily windows on rotating station schedules — policy escalation beyond the prior limited-hours and fixed-cap regime

The Insider: Ukrainian owners of confiscated property in occupied Mariupol are compensated at 70,000 rubles/m² while new housing on the same market sells at 170,000 rubles/m² — a 2.4× gap between the price the state pays to expropriate and the price it charges to resell, making the confiscation programme a transfer rather than a purchase (Sep 1 investigation, logged Sep 3). The confiscation COUNT is deliberately not restated here: 34,002 flagged addresses with 14,308 in Mariupol is BBC Verify Aug 7 and is already carried in the Mariupol history note.

KSE Institute August Chartbook: July export earnings $13.8bn (from $15.8bn in June), export volumes 7.0M bpd (from 7.6M) — a structural volume decline; OFZ issuance lowest since September 2022 with auctions suspended through at least September; Jan–Jul federal deficit 6.5tn rubles, 34% above the full-year target
Ukrainian strikes on the Lukoil Permnefteorgsintez refinery (Perm Krai) and Taganrog Airbase overnight Sep 6–7; second strike on the Sochi oil depot, repeating Sep 4

Drone strike destroys the Galaktika shopping centre and adjacent fuel station in occupied Mariupol overnight Sep 6–7 (Reuters photographs, Kyiv Post, Astra) — fourth Galaktika location destroyed in occupied Donetsk Oblast within a month (Makiivka Aug 9–10, Yenakiieve Aug 14, Donetsk Aug 16, Mariupol Sep 6–7); Astra identifies the destroyed station as reportedly the last Galaktika-brand fuel station in occupied Donetsk Oblast

Ukrainian General Staff reports a strike on the railway bridge across the North Crimean Canal near Vladyslavivka; GUR drone operators damage a Su-24 tactical bomber in occupied Crimea overnight Sep 6–7
Russian milblogger acknowledges the M-14 Rostov–Crimea highway remains under continuous Ukrainian drone pressure, contradicting occupation officials’ claims that the corridor is secure

HUR chief states Ukrainian strikes have contributed to a Russian federal budget deficit of $82bn, while assessing that Russia may retain resources through 2028 — the latter a counter-signal to the upward pressure narrative
